newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurds ready for second round of truce talks.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds ready for second round of truce talks.

text.p: Rival Iraqi Kurdish groups will meet in Ankara on Friday for a second round of U.S.-brokered talks aiming to make permanent a three-week ceasefire, the Turkish foreign ministry said.
"Our preparations are going on for the meeting tomorrow," a foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters on Thursday.

Delegations from Massoud Barzani's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Jalal Talabani's Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) agreed on extend the truce in late October at the first round of peace talks in Ankara.

U.S. diplomat Robert Pellletreau, who is overseeing the talks along with British and Turkish diplomats, brokered the ceasefire between Kurdish factions ahead of those talks following around two months of fighting.

Mediators say the talks are also aiming to solve key issues of contol of the the city of Arbil and sharing of revenues from a KDP oil trade on the Turkish border, as well as ways of prolonging the ceasefire.

"At the last meeting we discussed many things but agreed on ceasefire. (In northern Iraq) there has to be a solid truce and a mechanism to monitor it," said Safeen Dizayee, the KDP's representative in Ankara. The KDP delegation is expected to arrive in Ankara later on Thursday.
PUK representative Sazad Saib said they are ready for the talks, but was cagey about his expectations: "Let us wait and see," he said.
Barzani joined forces with Baghdad in late August to take Arbil from the PUK, prompting U.S missile strikes against targets in southern Iraq.
